title: A sales summary, two levels deep
prompt:
You are given an array of sales records, each `{ region, category, amount }`. Build a summary object where each key is a `region`, and each value is an object mapping `category` to the sum of `amount` for that region and category.

For example, two `West` records in `Widgets` and one in `Gadgets` become `{ "West": { "Widgets": <sum>, "Gadgets": <sum> } }`. A region that only ever appears with one category still produces an object, just with one key.
hints: `groupBy` hands you back an Object, keyed by whatever you grouped on — not an Array. Check `typeOf` on the result before deciding what to do with it next.

You need this shape twice: once to bucket by region, and again inside each bucket to bucket by category. Whatever turns an Object into another Object without leaving Object-land is what you want at both levels.
`map` expects an Array. Calling it directly on the result of `groupBy` is not a smaller version of the right answer — it does not run at all.

mustFail.why: calls map directly on the object groupBy returns, which is a hard engine error, not a smaller or partial result
stops after the first groupBy and sums straight across categories, losing the second level of the report entirely

explanation.approach: `groupBy` never returns an Array — it returns an Object whose keys are the grouping values and whose values are the Arrays of matching items. That means the next step in the chain has to be something that iterates an Object, which is `pluck` (Object to Array) or `mapObject` (Object to Object), never `map` (Array to Array). A two-level report just applies this twice: group by region into an Object of Arrays, then inside each Array group by category and reduce each bucket to a single number with `sum`.

snippets.label: Check the shape before you chain anything onto it
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ raw: typeOf(payload), grouped: typeOf(payload groupBy $.region) }
snippets.note: An Array goes in and an Object comes out. That one line decides everything after it: the next step has to be an object function, and reaching for `map` here is an error rather than a wrong answer.

snippets.label: What groupBy actually hands back
snippets.note: An Object, keyed by region, each value still the Array of full records that matched. Nothing has been summed yet.

snippets.label: Calling map on that Object
snippets.note: `UnexpectedFunctionCallTypesException`: map wants an Array and was handed an Object. This is not a wrong answer that runs — it does not run at all, which is exactly why it is easy to write without noticing: the mistake shows up as a stack trace, not a bad number.

snippets.label: mapObject, going Object to Object, is the shape that fits
snippets.note: This is one level of aggregation — a single total per region. It compiles and runs, but it throws away the category breakdown the report actually needs; West's Widgets and Gadgets are already merged into 140 before there is any chance to split them back out.

snippets.label: The full two-level chain
snippets.note: The inner `groupBy $.category mapObject ...` runs once per region, on that region's own Array of records, before its result becomes the value stored under `(region)`.

snippets.label: pluck is the Object-to-Array alternative, useful for a flatter report
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload groupBy $.region pluck ((lines, region) -> { region: region, total: sum(lines.amount) })
snippets.note: Same grouped Object, but `pluck` turns it into an Array of `{region, total}` rows instead of a nested Object. Neither `pluck` nor `mapObject` is `map` in disguise — each names what the input actually is.
